The Undercity, now known as the Ruins of Undercity, was the capital city of the Forsaken kingdom, located beneath the ruins of Capital City in Tirisfal Glades. Originally intended by Arthas Menethil to be the Scourge's seat of power in Lordaeron, the budding "Undercity" was abandoned when the death knight was recalled by the Lich King in the distant Northrend. During the Plaguelands civil war, Sylvanas Windrunner and the Forsaken rebels claimed the Undercity for their own, then spent years completing the twisted maze of catacombs the Scourge had begun constructing. It was much more defensible than the city above it.
Plagued by the Banshee Queen during the Battle for Lordaeron, its surface has since been cleansed by the efforts of the Desolate Council.

{{NPC||Varimathras|icon=Nathrezim}}{{KIA}} | languages = [[Gutterspeak]], [[Zombie (language)|Zombie]], [[Thalassian]], [[Common (language)|Common]], [[Orcish (language)|Orcish]], [[Goblin (language)|Goblin]], [[Taur-ahe]] | faiths = [[Cult of the Forgotten Shadow|Forgotten Shadow]] | affiliation = [[Forsaken (kingdom)|Forsaken kingdom]], [[Horde]] | faffiliation = [[Burning Legion]], [[Dreadlord Insurgents]] [[Scourge]] | loc = Beneath the [[Ruins of Lordaeron|Ruins of Capital City]], southern [[Tirisfal Glades]] | territory = Horde | status = Plagued''[[World of Warcraft: Exploring Azeroth: The Eastern Kingdoms]]'', pg. 116 }} {{QuoteWiki|Beneath the ruins of Lordaeron, the armies of the Forsaken plot and scheme.|[[Undercity (Fields of Honor)|TCG card]] description}} The '''Undercity''', now known as the '''Ruins of Undercity''', was the [[Capital city|capital]] [[city]] of the [[Forsaken (kingdom)|Forsaken kingdom]], located beneath the [[Ruins of Lordaeron|ruins]] of [[Capital City]] in [[Tirisfal Glades]]. Originally intended by [[Arthas Menethil]] to be the [[Scourge]]'s seat of power in [[Lordaeron]], the budding "Undercity" was abandoned when the [[death knight]] was recalled by the [[Lich King]] in the distant [[Northrend]]. During the [[Plaguelands civil war]], [[Sylvanas Windrunner]] and the [[Forsaken]] rebels claimed the Undercity for their own, then spent years completing the twisted maze of catacombs the Scourge had begun constructing.[[Game Guide/Undead|Races of World of Warcraft: Undead]] It was much more defensible than the city above it.''[[World of Warcraft: Exploring Azeroth: The Eastern Kingdoms]]'', pg. 110 [[New Plague|Plagued]] by the Banshee Queen during the [[Battle for Lordaeron]], its surface has since been cleansed[[The Remedy of Lordaeron]] by the efforts of the [[Desolate Council]].[[Eyes of the Wolf]][[Call to Lordaeron]] {{OTOC|550|215}} ==History== ===Origins=== {{Novel-section}} The Undercity was so named many years before the Forsaken claimed it as their own. Far beneath the [[Lordaeron's palace|palace]] of Lordaeron, the Undercity held the ancient crypts and catacombs of Lordaeron's royalty, as well as the city's dungeons and sewers. Although the Undercity was only intended for prisoners and the dead, the poorest of the Lordaeron people lived within. Now and then the guards would go down and make a sweep of the place in a desperate and ultimately futile attempt to clean it out. When the [[Alliance of Lordaeron]] captured [[Orgrim Doomhammer]], they sent him to the Undercity; sometime later he managed to escape and wandered for many years afterwards.''[[Arthas: Rise of the Lich King]]'', chapter 2 ===Legacy of the Damned=== {{WC3-section}} [[File:Ruins of Lordaeron Comic.jpg|thumb|The [[Forsaken]] moving into the [[Ruins of Lordaeron]].]] After [[Capital City]] was [[Scourging of Lordaeron|decimated]] by the [[Scourge]] in 20 [[ADP]],[[Arthas' Betrayal (WC3 Human)]] a small contingent of [[undead]] were left behind by [[Arthas Menethil|Prince Arthas Menethil]] to carve out a new "Undercity" beneath the ruined capital. Following the [[Battle of Mount Hyjal]] in 21 ADP, Arthas returned to the [[ruins of Lordaeron]] to rule over his undead subjects, annihilate the last pockets of human resistance, and oust the remaining [[dreadlord]]s who were unaware of the [[Burning Legion]]'s defeat. In the wake of [[Illidan Stormrage]]'s failed attempt to destroy the [[Frozen Throne]], however, the [[Lich King]] [[Ner'zhul]]'s powers began to wane, and Arthas had to leave Lordaeron to defend his master from the [[Illidari]]'s second assault.[[King Arthas (WC3 Undead)]] As the Lich King's control over the undead faltered, one group of undead broke away from the Scourge under the command of [[Sylvanas Windrunner]], who plotted with the [[Dreadlord Insurgents]] to destroy Arthas.[[A Kingdom Divided (WC3 Undead)]] During the [[Plaguelands civil war]] in 22 ADP, Sylvanas rallied the free-willed undead and lured Arthas into a trap, but the fallen prince managed to escape with the help of [[Kel'Thuzad]]. After Arthas escaped to [[Northrend]][[Sylvanas' Farewell (WC3 Undead)]] and eventually [[Ascension of the Lich King|ascended]] as the new Lich King, Lordaeron became a battlefield between the [[Dreadlord Insurgents]], [[Sylvanas' Forces]] and the [[Alliance resistance]]. Once they emerged victorious, the Banshee Queen proclaimed her faction of self-aware undead as the "[[Forsaken]]", then claimed the ruined capital city of Lordaeron as their own. Constructing their own bastion, far beneath the wrecked city, the Forsaken vowed to defeat the Scourge and drive Kel'Thuzad and his minions from the land.''[[World of Warcraft: Game Manual]]'', pg. 165 ===World of Warcraft=== {{wow-section}} By the Year 25 ADP, the royal crypts have been turned into a bastion of evil and undeath, where the Forsaken have worked to complete the Undercity's construction that the Scourge began. ===Wrath of the Lich King=== {{Wotlk-section}} {{Main|Battle for the Undercity}} [[File:Undercity.jpg|thumb|The Trade Quarter within the city.]] Following the disaster at [[Angrathar the Wrathgate]], the Banshee Queen was forced to flee the Undercity, where [[Grand Apothecary Putress]] had sided with [[Varimathras]] and the [[Burning Legion]] to orchestrate a coup d'état.[[Herald of War]] When [[Jaina Proudmoore]] brought these news to [[Varian Wrynn]], the king of [[Stormwind (kingdom)|Stormwind]] greeted Sylvanas's explanation with suspicion but also saw an opportunity: since the Undercity was not under the Horde's control, perhaps it was time for the Alliance to reclaim the old nation of Lordaeron.{{Ref WoWCV1|180|181}} Consequently, both the Horde and the Alliance launched separate offensives against the Undercity. [[Warchief]] [[Thrall]], along with Sylvanas and [[Vol'jin]], led the assault to kill Varimathras within the city, while King Varian and his forces stormed through the city's sewers in search of Putress.[[The Battle For The Undercity]] After the rebellion leaders paid the price for their treachery, King Varian was not satisfied and was disgusted by the condition of the once great city, which he had known since childhood. Even worse, they also discovered dozens of mutilated and defiled human corpses, on which the [[Royal Apothecary Society]] had experimented on the [[New Plague]] to kill them all. Before a catastrophic battle could unfold, Jaina intervened by freezing the combatants solid and teleporting all Alliance forces out of the Undercity, or both factions would have destroyed each other.''[[Exploring Azeroth: Northrend]]'', pg. 145 In the aftermath, Warchief Thrall sent a legion of [[Kor'kron Guard]] led by [[Bragor Bloodfist]] to occupy the Undercity, guarding it from threats outside and from any that may remain within following the conflict. ===Stormrage=== {{novel-section}} During the [[War Against the Nightmare]], Undercity was attacked by the [[Emerald Nightmare]]'s mists and shadowy warriors. The Banshee Queen, half of the Forsaken and all Horde representatives were tormented by the nightmares.''[[Stormrage]]'', chapter 18 ===Cataclysm=== {{Cata-section}} [[File:Lordaeron Ruins3.jpg|thumb|The [[Ruins of Lordaeron]] in {{g|cata}}.]] Prior to the [[Cataclysm (event)|Cataclysm]] in 28 ADP, the Undercity felt massive quakes.''[[The Shattering: Prelude to Cataclysm]]'', chapter 32 After the [[Battle for Andorhal]], the [[death knight]] [[Koltira Deathweaver]] was pulled by a hooked chain through a portal to the Undercity, where [[Sylvanas Windrunner]] would attempt to purge him of his compassion for [[Thassarian]] and make him more of a servant of the [[Horde]] - more specifically, a servant of Sylvanas and the Forsaken.[[The Reckoning (Western Plaguelands)]] ===Warlords of Draenor=== {{wod-section}} By the Year 31 ADP, the [[Kor'kron]] guards had left the Undercity, leaving only [[Bragor Bloodfist]] as the "Hand of Warchief" there. Under odd circumstances, the body of [[Overseer Kraggosh]] was found in a cage. ===Legion=== {{Legion-section}} [[File:The Apothecarium.jpg|thumb|The [[Apothecarium]] in the Undercity.]] During the [[Third invasion of the Burning Legion]] in 32 ADP, when [[Lilian Voss]] dispatched the [[Adventurer|Shadowblade]] to go after the [[Homunculus|homunculi]] who infiltrated the Undercity.[[Hiding In Plain Sight (Alliance)]] Over the years since [[Koltira Deathweaver]] was imprisoned, the [[Knights of the Ebon Blade]] made several attempts to negotiate with Sylvanas for his release, but she refused them all. After [[Thassarian]] made a personal request to the Deathlord, Koltira was successfully broken out of the [[Apothecarium]] in [[Undercity]] and became a champion of the Ebon Blade.[[A Personal Request]][[Champion: Koltira Deathweaver]] ===Before the Storm=== {{Novel-section}} After the [[Argus Campaign]], the [[Desolate Council]] governed the city in Sylvanas Windrunner's absence, who longed to return home but couldn't due to her Warchief duties in Orgrimmar. Still, Nathanos kept tabs and informed Sylvanas of the ongoings in the city. The Desolate Council hosted a remembrance ceremony in the Undercity to honor the [[Forsaken]] that died during the [[third invasion of the Burning Legion]]. [[Alonsus Faol]] later traveled to the Undercity to relay King Anduin's missives to [[Vellcinda Benton]] and Warchief Sylvanas, which concerned the proposal of the [[Gathering]]. Upon hearing this, Sylvanas did come back and informed the Desolate Council of the specifics of the Gathering.''[[Before the Storm]]'' ===Battle for Azeroth=== {{bfa-section}} Prior to the [[Battle for Lordaeron]] in 33 ADP, Undercity's civilians were evacuated to [[Orgrimmar]] while the [[Gallywix' Boys]]'s [[Bilgewater Blastmasters]] loaded the streets with [[New Plague|Blight]] barrels and explosives as they were tasked. In the meantime, the city was infiltrated by the [[Druid of the claw|druids of the claw]] and [[SI:7]] agents, though they were quickly dispatched by Horde soldiers.[[The Battle for Lordaeron]] Instead of losing the battle, Sylvanas ordered the explosives to be activated flooding the upper and lower cities with plague, which killed both the living and the dead, making the capital uninhabitable.''[[World of Warcraft: Exploring Azeroth: The Eastern Kingdoms]]'', pg. 116 In the aftermath, the Forsaken [[refugee]]s established camps on top of the [[Gates of Orgrimmar]] and inside the capital's streets. ===Shadowlands=== {{Sl-section}} In Year 36 ADP, the [[Desolate Council]] and the [[adventurer]]s used a plague eater from [[Maldraxxus]][[Return to Brill]] to manifest the [[Amalgam]], which cleansed the surface from the [[New Plague]][[The Remedy of Lordaeron]] while the Undercity itself remained inaccessible.[[The Desolate Council]] ==Geography== Rivers of poisonous sludge flow through all avenues of the vast Undercity. The toxic fumes and fetid odors permeating every corner of the stronghold have made it a place almost unbearable for the living members of the Horde. Yet for [[Sylvanas Windrunner]] and her cursed followers, the Undercity has become a much-needed refuge in a world where her kind is still feared and hunted. The Undercity has many secret routes used by the Banshee Queen to move about the city in secret, and [[Nathanos Blightcaller]] suspects that there are a few such passageways kept hidden even from him.''[[Dark Mirror]]'' ===Map and quarters=== [[File:WorldMap-Undercity.jpg|thumb|Map of the Undercity.]] The city is made up of roughly symmetrical quarters arranged around a circular center. *'''[[Ruins of Lordaeron]]''' - Outdoors area beyond and including the entry area. *'''[[Trade Quarter|The Trade Quarter]]''' - The city center at the bottom elevator exits. *'''[[Magic Quarter|The Magic Quarter]]''' - Northeast from the Trade Quarter. *'''[[Rogues' Quarter|The Rogues' Quarter]]''' - Southeast from the Trade Quarter. *'''[[Apothecarium|The Apothecarium]]''' - Southwest from the Trade Quarter. *'''[[War Quarter|The War Quarter]]''' - Northwest from the Trade Quarter. *'''[[Royal Quarter|The Royal Quarter]]''' - South from the Apothecarium entrance. *'''[[Sewers|The Sewers]]''' - Through a tunnel west of city. *'''[[Canals (Undercity)|The Canals]]''' - Interspace between the different quarters. ===Points of interest=== {{Main|Undercity points of interest}} [[File:OrbofTranslocationUC.jpg|thumb|The [[Orb of Translocation]] outside of the Undercity.]] *The [[Bank]] in the very heart of the city, in the middle of the Trade Quarter. *The [[Bat Handler]] stands in the southwestern part of the Trade Quarter. *The City Hall in the northeastern edge of the Trade Quarter. *The [[Auction House]] is located in the circular area that leads between the Trade Quarter and the rest of the city. *The [[mailbox]] is located on the north side of the upper rim of the Trade Quarter. Mailboxes are now also located near the auctioneers. ===Orb of Translocation=== Since the release of ''[[The Burning Crusade]]'', players with the expansion are able to access an [[Orb of Translocation]] to the [[Silvermoon City]] palace, making it easy for anyone to travel between the two cities without having to go through the [[Plaguelands]]. The translocator works both ways. The Undercity orb is located in a newly opened city section west off the main part of the [[Ruins of Lordaeron]]. The translocator teleports you to the [[Inner Sanctum (Silvermoon City)|Inner Sanctum]] of the [[Sunfury Spire]] within [[Silvermoon City]]. It cannot be used by the Alliance. ===King Terenas' tomb=== Although the memorial to [[King Terenas]] appears to be a stone tomb, it was shown in ''[[Warcraft III: Reign of Chaos]]'' that after his death, Terenas was {{wplink|Cremation|cremated}}. Furthermore, the urn containing his ashes was used to resurrect the [[Lich]] [[Kel'Thuzad]]. It is unknown what happened to the King's remains after this point. The memorial was crafted by the [[Alliance]] humans who once inhabited the old city, who risked everything to ensure that the memory of Lordaeron's last true king would not be forgotten.[[Ask CDev#Ask CDev Answers - Round 4]] ===The throne room=== [[File:Throneroom.jpg|thumb|The [[Imperial chamber|throne room]] of Lordaeron.]] When you stand in the [[Imperial chamber|throne room]], at least in the center of the circle on the floor, with the ambient sound turned all the way up, in the background noises you can hear small clips of [[Arthas]], [[Medivh]], and [[King Terenas]]. For those who wish to hear this without venturing into the Undercity, the ambient sound file is located at (WoW Directory)\Data\Sound\Ambience\WMOAmbience\UnderCityThorneRoom.wav. If you look closely on the floor of the throne room, near the foot of the throne, you can see a small trail of blood that was left by the crown as it rolled onto the floor. By the same token, in the outer hall leading into the throne room, one can hear the celebration of Arthas' return by Lordaeron's citizens. The floor is littered with dead rose petals, the same ones seen showering Arthas during the cutscene in ''Warcraft III''. When standing by the bell outside of the throne room you can hear it ringing. ==Notable characters== {{Main|Undercity NPCs}} ==Travel connections== ===Flight=== ;{{Horde}} [[The Sepulcher]], [[Silverpine Forest]] ;{{Horde}} [[Forsaken High Command]], [[Silverpine Forest]] ;{{Horde}} [[Brill]], [[Tirisfal Glades]] ;{{Horde}} [[The Bulwark]], [[Tirisfal Glades]] ;{{Horde}} [[Tarren Mill]], [[Hillsbrad Foothills]] ;{{Horde}} [[Hammerfall]], [[Arathi Highlands]] ;{{Horde}} [[Revantusk Village]], [[Hinterlands]] ;{{Horde}} [[New Kargath]], [[Badlands]] ;{{Horde}} [[Sandy Beach]], [[Shimmering Expanse]] {{cata-inline}} ;{{Neutral}} [[Light's Hope Chapel]] ===Zeppelin=== ;{{Horde}} [[Orgrimmar]], [[Durotar]] ;{{Horde}} [[Grom'gol Base Camp]], [[Northern Stranglethorn]] ;{{Horde}} [[Vengeance Landing]], [[Howling Fjord]] {{wotlk-inline}} ===Teleport=== ;{{Horde}} [[Silvermoon City]], [[Eversong Woods (Burning Crusade)|Eversong Woods]] {{bc-inline}} ([[Orb of Translocation]] from the [[Ruins of Lordaeron]]) ;{{Neutral}} [[Dark Portal|The Dark Portal]], [[Blasted Lands]] (from the [[Magic Quarter]]) ==Quests== {{main|Undercity quests}} {{See also|Undercity questing guide}} ==In the RPG== {{RPG-section}} To the southeastern [[Tirisfal Glades]] you will find the [[Forsaken]]'s capital of Undercity. This maze was originally the crypts and dungeons beneath [[Lordaeron (kingdom)|Lordaeron]]'s [[Capital City|capital]], but the Forsaken have added to their city with tunnels, caverns, structures and the like.''[[Lands of Conflict]]'', pg. 107 The city is protected by 13 mysterious [[black iron golem]]s, metal juggernauts of unknown origin.''[[Magic & Mayhem]]'', pg. 199 - 200; 206 ===History=== Lordaeron's capital city stood for centuries, a monument to humanity's might. In the [[Third War]], [[Prince Arthas]] slew his father [[King Terenas]] in Lordaeron's [[Imperial chamber|throne room]] and ransacked the city. He planned to use Lordaeron as his capital on this continent and ordered his minions to expand the catacombs beneath the city. Then the [[Lich King]] summoned Arthas to [[Northrend]] and the work was left uncompleted. During Arthas' exodus, [[Sylvanas Windrunner]] broke free of the Lich King's control and took many [[banshee]]s and other [[undead]] with her. With [[Varimathras]]' assistance she defeated the [[dreadlord]]s that controlled the city and set her newly dubbed Forsaken to finish Arthas' job in the dungeons. The Forsaken carved Undercity and now rule the surrounding countryside.''[[Lands of Conflict]]'', pg. 109 Warchief [[Thrall]] and [[Cairne Bloodhoof]] sent [[Ambassador Galavosh]], a mighty shaman, to Undercity to keep an eye on the Forsaken and make sure they are honest about their intention to dismiss their evil tendencies. He is investigating the [[Royal Apothecary Society]] who are based in the [[Apothecarium]]. They mess around with potions, venoms, diseases, and other alchemy. Their leader, [[Master Apothecary Faranell]], sends many Forsaken out on missions to gather strange objects that must be ingredients for something. Sylvanas Windrunner, once the elven ranger captain of [[Quel'Thalas (kingdom)|Quel'Thalas]], claims to drive the Forsaken to defeat the Scourge and establish their own place on [[Azeroth]], but what that place may be, and whether or not it includes living beings is not known. Varimathras serves as Sylvanas' lieutenant and closest advisor. Formerly one of Sylvanas' greatest enemies, Varimathras betrayed the Scourge and the [[Burning Legion]] and defected to Sylvanas' side. He is in charge of Undercity's defense, and his forces range across Tirisfal, eliminating all those they see as a threat. The dreadlord is tasked with eradicating the [[Scarlet Crusade]], a fanatical group of humans who seek to destroy all undead.''[[Lands of Conflict]]'', pg. 107 - 108 ===Geography=== Undercity is an extension of the crypts and dungeons originally beneath Lordaeron's capital city. The Forsaken dredged out complex catacombs and caverns. The place is dark, smells like dead people and has an evil feel. [[Spider]]s, [[ooze]]s and other subterranean creatures occupy the distant passages. You could wander for weeks in Undercity and never see everything.''[[Lands of Conflict]]'', pg. 108 - 109 ==Notes and trivia== ;Lore *[[Clayton Backston]] had a garden in the Undercity.[[Zandalari Justice]] *A [[Moat Monster|tentacle monster]] lived in the Undercity moat, fed by the Forsaken to defend it. *[[Report from the Frontlines: Undercity]], a book found in [[Acherus: The Ebon Hold]], reveals that the Undercity at one point had Scourge infiltrators within the city walls. *The Undercity was once infiltrated by [[SI:7]] - [[Renzik "The Shiv"]] who then provided sketches of the city and the Royal Quarter to his organization; as well as their leader [[Mathias Shaw]] who entered through the throne room.''[[World of Warcraft: Exploring Azeroth: The Eastern Kingdoms]]'', pg. 110, 113 *[[Sylvanas Windrunner]] seems to find the Undercity appealing to the eye, in spite of its rotting guards, necromantic constructs and mysterious green fluids. When she, [[Thrall]] and the player invaded the Undercity during the [[The Battle For The Undercity (Horde)|struggle to retake it]], she exclaimed, "What have they done to my beautiful city?" ;Gameplay *The Undercity doesn't have a [[Fruit vendors|fruit vendor]]. *There are two zeppelin towers within fairly short walking distance of the Ruins of Lordaeron, one offers flights to [[Orgrimmar]], [[Durotar]] and [[Grom'Gol Base Camp]] in [[Northern Stranglethorn]], the other to [[Vengeance Landing]] in the [[Howling Fjord]] in [[Northrend]]. *Do not worry about falling into the green liquid; it is harmless, and you may get out of it by finding a sewer pipe exit (exterior of the Undercity) or a small stairway (interior of the Undercity). You can even fish on it, but you won't catch anything magnificent. *Using [[Detect Invisibility]] or a similar ability within the Ruins of Lordaeron (within the walls but before entering the throne room), it is possible to see low-level undead mobs (each named "[[Lordaeron Citizen]]"), similar to the [[Unseen]] in [[Duskwood]]. *At one time there was a glitch in the game, so that a character running towards the opposing wall of a descending elevator would fall through the world, into [[Stonetalon Mountains]], and then the [[Alterac Mountains]]. This may suggest that Blizzard used a vertical system for zone placement in addition to the existing horizontal one, creating another reason for not allowing flying mounts in classic content. *The Undercity elevators are considered an [[elevator boss]] during the original experience as it took many player's lives due to how the doors close immediately as the elevator starts going down without delay, allowing a slim chance for a player to walk to the elevator and fall to their death. This resulted in many deaths in {{g|hc}}. *Guards spawned from civilians are only level 65. *A [[tauren]] riding on a [[kodo]] [[mount]] has to dismount to enter the elevators through the throne room. *The [[Kor'kron Overseer (Undercity)|orcish guards]] who temporarily replaced most of the Forsaken guards and Abominations inside Undercity also had their own flavor of text responses when players interacted with them when finding out something like class or profession trainers. They had distinct reservations about Undercity, from its inn to its cooking, and sometimes had hostile responses, particularly for players wishing to find the warlock trainer. ;Other *Though from the outside players see many towers and rooftops, they were originally, in fact, nothing more than an illusion. The former Lordaeron capital was sparsely decorated in-game with only the courtyard, translocater room and tomb being an actual part of the former structure. The game designers did not intend for anyone to see Lordaeron from above, or get to other parts, just to walk through it. This was changed in ''[[World of Warcraft: Cataclysm]]'', and the ruins of Lordaeron are now fully built. [[File:Undercity balconies.jpg|thumb|The upper balconies of the Undercity.]] *Balconies above the inner circle parts of the [[War Quarter]], [[Mage Quarter]], [[Rogues' Quarter]], and [[Apothecarium]] can be seen while flying in and out of the city by taxi. These empty balconies, aside from a single [[Food Crate|food crate]], are on the same level as the [[Trade Quarter]] and are connected by footbridges that span above the corridors leading to and from the Trade Quarter and the outer quarters. These balconies and their connecting bridges can actually be seen on the map of Undercity. They cannot be reached on foot, but a mage can use [[Slow Fall (ability)]], a priest can use [[Levitate]], and an Engineer can use a [[Parachute Cloak]] to reach these balconies. From the top of the [[Sewers|sewer]] tunnel where [[Vampire Bat|vampire bats]] pass, a player can activate either any one of these, mount up, run and jump, aiming to the left of the tunnel, to land on the balconies above the [[War Quarter]]. [[#Undercity's Upper floor|Video of how to reach them]]. **During the alpha, there were passages that led up there from the Canals. *There are portions of the Undercity where effects from ''Warcraft III'' were deliberately inserted into the game as ambient sounds. These areas are the throne room, the hallway directly outside of it, and even the bell tower located just at its entrance. Near the bell, you will hear the churchbells ringing when Arthas returns to Lordaeron before he becomes a death knight. **In the hall before the throne room, there are still scattered rose petals on the cobblestones from Arthas' return. In the throne room itself, a slight trail of blood — from when [[Terenas Menethil II|Terenas']] crown rolled on the floor after Arthas murdered him — can be seen near the throne. What is most chilling is that the room echoes with Arthas' own voice saying the words, "Succeeding you, father," his words before he murdered his own father. *On the in-game map of the Undercity, the emblem of the Scourge is used instead of the regular Forsaken emblem. *The Undercity was originally called "[[Necropolis]]" in early concept maps for ''[[World of Warcraft]]''.[[:File:ABE - Lordaeron and Khaz Modan map.jpg]][[:File:WoWCE - Lordaeron.jpg]] The quest [[Delivery to Silverpine Forest]] mentions a Necropolis while talking about Undercity, which may be a remnant of the alpha stage considering the ID of the quest. ''[[Before the Storm]]'' refers to the Undercity as a "subterranean necropolis".''[[Before the Storm]]'', chapter 12 **The city's layout may be a remnant of this, as its circular design with four distinct quadrants is very reminiscent of the necropoli [[Naxxramas]] and [[Acherus: The Ebon Hold|Acherus]]. *It took several months for [[Jose Aello Jr.]] and [[Dana Jan]] to create the Undercity during the development of WoW. According to [[Johnathan Staats|John Staats]], [[Chris Metzen]] wanted the Undercity to just be a disheveled, wrecked, and ugly-looking city where everything was split up, while the artists wanted more of a habitable hub as opposed to a randomized maze (partially because many of the artists had nightmares from a city in the [[Diablo franchise|''Diablo'' universe]] where the player had to run everywhere to get to all of the NPCs they needed to talk to). Eventually, the level designers won out on that argument.{{Ref web|url=https://countdowntoclassic.com/2018/08/20/episode-63-the-making-of-world-of-warcraft-with-vanilla-dev-john-staats/|title=Countdown To Classic: Episode #63 – The Making Of World Of Warcraft With Vanilla Dev, John Staats (around 2:28:20)|date=2018-08-20|accessdate=2018-09-24}} ==Gallery== File:Canals.jpg|[[Canals (Undercity)|The Canals]] File:Magic Quarter.jpg|[[Magic Quarter]] File:Rogues' Quarter.jpg|[[Rogues' Quarter]] File:Royal Quarter.jpg|[[Royal Quarter]] File:Sewers.jpg|[[Sewers|The Sewers]] File:Trade Quarter.jpg|[[Trade Quarter]] File:War Quarter.jpg|[[War Quarter]] File:undercitymapmanual.jpg|Map of Undercity in ''[[World of Warcraft: Game Manual]]''. No longer accessible for players, unless you speak with [[Zidormi]] in [[Tirisfal Glades]].}} *{{Patch 6.0.2|note=[[Kor'kron Guard]]s replaced by [[Undercity Guardian]]s.}} *{{Patch 3.0.2|note=Abomination Guards replaced by Kor'kron Guards.}} *{{Patch 1.4.0|note=Patrolling scouts that can see through stealth and invisibility have been added to the Undercity.}} *{{Patch 0.6|note=Undercity had undergone layout changes.}} ==See also== *[[Undercity (Fields of Honor)]], TCG card ==References== {{Reflist}} ==External links== {{Elinks-zone|1497}} {{Undercity}} {{Tirisfal Glades}} {{Eastern Kingdoms}} {{New Horde}} {{ExpansionHub}} [[Category:Undercity| ]] [[Category:Forsaken territories]] [[Category:Cities]] [[Category:Burial sites]] [[Category:Horde settlements]]
